response: The EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), effective since May 2018, fundamentally reshaped data privacy by applying to any organization processing EU residents' data globally. Key provisions include rights to access, erasure, and data portability, requiring explicit consent and mandating 72-hour breach reporting, with violations penalties reaching 4% of global revenue or 20 million euros. Major fines have been issued to tech giants—Meta 1.2 billion euros, Amazon 746 million euros, and Google over 200 million euros—while the regulation has inspired similar laws worldwide like California's CCPA and Brazil's LGPD. Although criticized for compliance burdens and inconsistent enforcement, GDPR established data privacy as a fundamental right and set the global standard for data protection.
